Otherwise, she will exercise in the yard for about two hours, then copy scriptures or read in her study until noon. She then goes to the nearby commercial district for lunch.
During her lunch break, villagers will often approach her, asking for help with farm work or to settle some trouble (there is a consensus among the locals that her help is first-come-first-served), and what's most astonishing is that she will agree to help them after eating. You could say she spends most of her afternoon helping the villagers, and on the rare occasion she has free time, she will head to the snowy mountains in search of something more exciting.
Usually, her dinner is willingly provided by the villagers who borrowed her assistance, or she'll simply have something on the road. Then, she goes for a stroll by Lake Silberneherze before returning to her residence and calling it a day.
Yes, Miss Degenbrecher, the living legend who left an unbroken record in Kazimierz is now living the simple life here in Kjerag. This only whets our curiosity about her attitude toward life, but she was unwilling to share her opinion. After the writer was hung by a wooden pole on the wall outside her residence, we were forced to take a different approach. After interviewing some random neighboring villagers, we have selected a few valuable comments from them. Hopefully, our readers can get to know her better this way.

'Degenbrecher? She's a good person! Just ask around, there's no one here who hasn't received her help! You definitely have to write that down. No clue what this Kazimierz thing everyone keeps mentioning is, but she's definitely a good Kjerag girl!'
——An old man enjoying the shade under a tree
'Miss Degenbrecher? Oh, she's an honorary member of our Anglers Association. At first, we thought someone like her wouldn't be interested, but one day she spent the entire afternoon with us by an ice hole, and it was then I knew she was one of us. Go ask the fellas who're always at Lake Silberneherze. Everyone knows her, she's our idol.'
——A young angler
'Degenbrecher? To be honest, I was wary when she first joined us. After all, she pretty much took my position. But afterwards I stopped caring, yeah? Spend long enough with her, and you'll realize that despite how she looks, she really does care, deep down. There's no doubt she's an indispensable member of the Silverash family.'
——An Itra with a strange scent
'Can Kjerag can satisfy her? That is but the preliminary question. You will soon discover that what gives her cause to leave or stay is not the satisfaction she feels, but whether her environment makes sense to her. I am pleased to note that Kjerag does indeed, and I believe her attitude towards it represents a sort of simple, yet sharp, perspective on this place. I can only hope that she finds the future Kjerag just as coherent.'
——A Feline who asked to conceal his identity
.....
——Excerpt from the March 1098 issue of 'Kjerag Newsletter' second edition

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
Degenbrecher stands halfway up the mountain, turning around to view the scenery she has grown a little tired of, and recalls the first time she faced an avalanche.
She had no choice but to face Kjeragandr's 'turnover'—the local parlance for an avalanche—to save a couple who could not escape in time. It was an interesting experience for her, and she realized for the first time how she could simultaneously wrestle with nature and have fun.
Since then, you could always find her in the rescue team whenever an avalanche occurred in Kjerag, and as such she has become a hero to many of the locals.
Honestly, I'm only trying to entertain myself, she thinks.
These days, Kjerag's avalanche warning system is more than sufficient. The day before one occurs, the monitoring center sounds an alarm to warn the residents and pedestrians at the foot of the mountain to evacuate, and the mountain is closed to everyone and anyone—with her as the sole exception.
When she sees the locals watching her walk into the snowy mounts with surprise in their eyes, she thinks she did not come here to win or lose.
For her, there is no victory or defeat against an avalanche. After all, what even counts as a win? To survive? If so, then naturally she's on a winning streak. But if requires her to cut down her foe, then she has never once succeeded.
But this does not dishearten her, for she finds it quite enjoyable to challenge something she cannot defeat. Besides, as long as she lives, she can try again and again. And perhaps one day, she might just succeed?
Even so, the Kazimierz knights had regarded her as an insurmountable wall, and not just that. Once they concluded she was unbeatable, they gave up entirely on trying to score a victory, with their bouts somehow ending up about testing their skills against hers by the number of blows they could take before falling.
A wave of white snow rises from the mountaintop and rolls downward.
She looks up, thinking of Enciodes and his hooded friend.
She thinks that what they face is just like the avalanche in front of her, or what those knights saw her as.
She pulls out the swordbreakers stuck in the snow, and launches herself towards the wave.
They always seem to make the same choice as her.

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
Aspirations.
For the orphan living out on the streets, it was survival and having a good meal.
To achieve this goal, she wielded her worn-out swordbreakers and killed her way from Leithanien to Kazimierz, turning herself from an obscure competition knight into a champion.
Everyone she met on the way told her that survival doesn't count as an aspiration, that one's desires should be more complex than that. So many were so insistent that she became a little curious.
As a result, the Leithanian dark horse tried out many of their aspirations—their corrupt, intoxicating, infeasible lifestyles—she has tried it all.
She has also met those with so-called nobler inclinations.
But in doing so, she carefully realized that all their desires ultimately boil down to keeping themselves or the people around them alive, and to have a good meal afterward. It was then that she decided that Kazimierz did not hold the answer she was looking for.
And so the nation's champion chose to be exiled. By the way, the GCC probably still doesn't realize that if they hadn't sought her out, she'd never actually planned on winning a third time.
The conflict with Darksteel did indeed introduce unprecedented danger to her, and at the time she had two thoughts. One was to ask Darksteel what kind of aspirations someone as strong as them might have, and the second was that if her skills were lacking, then there really wasn't anything wrong with dying on the spot. Kazimierz was just that boring.
In the end, neither happened, and instead she met a young noble who claimed to hail from Kjerag.
You seem to be curious about how Enciodes convinced me to go with him at first. It was nothing special, he was just the first person I couldn't fully comprehend. And now, there are many more like him around me.
I don't understand you, Enciodes, or some of the others on this landship any more than you understand me.
You may find it hard to comprehend that I lack any aspirations, but do you people really have something you're striving for? All you do is to piece together the wishes of others into a huge fortress, then convince yourself that building it is a dream of your own.
Let's say I ask you now, what do you want to do? Can you think of anything that isn't just realizing the desires of someone else?
If you could trade your life to realize your dream, people like you probably wouldn't hesitate for a second, as if you were born just for that.
I've seen too many avaricious people drown in their own desires, as well as too many tragic deaths of those who did no wrong and only wanted to live. I've also seen many who managed to realize their desires and obtain the life they aspired to. But people like you, I've yet to see how your lives end.
And that's why I chose to go with him, and why I stand before you.
Just do whatever you want, and I'll make sure you live.

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
Degenbrecher is almost done packing her luggage. She stands up in the originally unremarkable living room, and looks around to confirm she didn't miss anything.
Going to Rhodes Island is just a relatively long vacation, so there shouldn't be a need to bring anything special, she thinks as she plans to take a final look at Lake Silberneherze from the window.
As she walks across the floor in the middle of the room, her footsteps make a different sound than they do elsewhere. Hollow echoes remind her there is something beneath the floorboards. She pauses for a moment. Of course she knows what lies underneath—the hilt of a greatsword, the very same one she used in Kazimierz. This also brings back a few memories of the past.
During her escape, the weapon was actually broken in two after blocking a Darksteel arrow. Back then, she threw the blade in reciprocation and took the hilt with her—after all, she had no other weapons then. Until she arrived at Kjerag and got her swordbreakers crafted by the Karlan Trade artisans. Naturally, she stopped using her greatsword.
And as for why, she once told Sharp that it was because Kjerag was too cramped for it. She often repeats this to others while imagining a future where she might need it. Which is why she decided to stash it under the floorboards in the first place.
However, she realizes now that even on the night she knew she was about to face Kjerag's biggest crisis yet, it never once came to mind. She had completely forgotten it existed until today. If not for her coincidental footsteps, she might not have realized it even after arriving at Rhodes Island.
'I suppose if Kjerag was too cramped, then Rhodes Island might not have space for it either.'
She thinks for a moment, then suddenly chuckles for some reason before walking towards the window.
She will probably never need to use that greatsword ever again.

lore.title: Profile
lore.text: Blaze, an elite Rhodes Island Operator, has demonstrated professional combat skills and tactical decisionmaking in mobile operations, annihilation, and raids. Now commanded by Amiya, she is a staple for when battles get tough.

lore.title: Clinical Analysis
lore.text:
Imaging tests reveal blurry outlines of this operator's internal organs, clouded with abnormal dark spots. Her circulatory system shows an abnormally high rate of Originium particulate matter, with other signs of Oripathy infection, we can confirm that the Operator is Infected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 16%
Operator Blaze has clear signs of Infection, with crystals deposited mainly on the trunk perhaps due to blood circulation.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.24u/L
Due to frequent contact with Originium products and participation in multiple Originium-rich areas, etc., Blaze's condition is in a dangerous state of development. Medics can only try to control the progression of Oripathy, but Blaze is not willing to leave the battlefield.
For some of Rhodes Island's elite operators, their responsibilities are given higher priority than their own physical condition.

Blaze, the next time you don't bring protective gear on the mission, I will have Dr. Kal'tsit forbid you from consuming alcoholic beverages.--Y.P., Medic Operator

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
[Originium Arts Overview]
'Actually, there's not much to it. Look, you got your one palm over here, and your other palm over there. Then you bring them together, and squeeze the air out from between them. That's pretty much what I do.'
Blaze generally uses language like this when describing her Originium Arts, which may make it easier to understand the nature of her abilities, but tells very little to those who are trying to research and classify Originium Arts.
Operator Blaze's Originium Arts can best be understood as the ability to rapidly heat gases within a specified area, though there obviously is a limit to how high she can raise this temperature, which she describes as 'approximately super-hot degrees.'
She cannot directly act upon objects, cannot exceed a certain range, and sometimes is unable to even cause direct damage. Her Arts is very restrictive in terms of the types of materials and receptors that can be acted upon.
Nevertheless, through continuous testing and training, she has honed her Arts in a way that greatly eclipses the complexity and efficacy of the original mode of use.
Whether using the rise of hot air as a buffer, using the rapid expansion of air around her to generate thrust, or by supercompressing a specific amount of air to create a temperature differential capable of causing a small-scale explosion, Blaze has thoroughly understood how to utilize her Arts.
She is also capable of using her own blood to enhance the effect of her Originium Arts, with a greater usage of blood corresponding to a greater increase in efficacy.
Though sometimes mistaken for a Caster, all illusions of such are quickly dispelled when she approaches them with her heated chainsaw.

'Look, what the hell did they decide to write here? Just look at that chainsaw. Do Casters lug stuff like that around? No no, is there anything about her that says 'Caster' to you?!'
-A fire-based Caster who has chosen not to reveal their identity

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
Among Rhodes Island's elite Operators, Blaze may indeed be the one with the most exposure. Anything else notwithstanding, her capricious, explosive personality and her likely-to-cause-collateral-damage combat skills have given her a degree of notoriety.
Despite this, Blaze has an almost perfect track record for completing her tasks. Among the Operators who struggle on the front lines, Blaze is considered as one of the most dedicated.
Nevertheless, regardless of whether the missions she was deployed to all happened to require such firepower, or because Dr. Kal'tsit deployed her specifically knowing her capacities, most of the missions that Blaze participates in are worth solving using these rather... unrestrained methods.
Literally, by erasing the source of the conflict, whether it's a dispute over Originium, ownership of a building, criminal activity, etc., there won't be any conflict remaining.
This doesn't mean that Blaze will, like some Operators, cause trouble for her fellow Operators or even be forced to act independently. Her ability to work as part of a team is also one-of-a-kind. In fact, a team with her as the main attacker can safely focus on supporting, defending, and completing other mission objectives, because Blaze can single-handed absorb all the combat pressure for them.
Would any team refuse a proposition like that?
As a matter of fact, yes. Quite a few, actually. Because Blaze's techniques and tactics are often risky and sudden, even if she is capable of achieving the greatest results, only the most capable of team members are able to keep up with her.
'Please enter freefall from 300 meters,' she will often say.
While she reassures them, 'Don't worry, I'll catch you,' stuff like that is not well-received by the faint of heart.
Over time, Rhodes Island has come to trust the young and enthusiastic elite, though not enough to treat her as a role model.
Just don't. Whatever you do, don't try to become another Blaze.
However, trust does not only come from the recognition of strength.
Blaze is committed in fighting for the rights and interests of the Infected, never wavering in her convictions.
She is firmly on the side of the Infected, and stands with all who fight for a just cause.
'You know she's trustworthy because she puts her life on the line for you.'

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
[Classified Log]
There's nothing special about elite Operators. Or perhaps I should say, how 'special' can the already special become?
Granted, any Operator may have quite a strong personal ability, but in the face of an entire city-state or a warship... facing the war machines continuously generated through the industrial capacity of an entire country, what hope does an Operator have?
To keep things simple, if three Apostolic knights are charging at you with miniguns, what kind of person would you have to be to deal with that kind of attack?
Having that said, an elite Operator will always work harder than the average Operator.
Even if one's strength can only make so much of a difference, each step taken indeed does help.
If you aren't able to deal enough damage to a target, study the structure of the weapon more, and work with the engineers to find ways of improving it. Train, train, and train more to wield heavier and stronger equipment.
If you aren't durable enough for the job, or if you hurt yourself with your own Arts, find a way to overcome it. Bring more medicine, install a special pacemaker installed by a friend, get back onto your feet even if your head is spinning, and join the battle again.
If your combat skills still have deficiencies, then throw yourself into the most brutal battles, and make up for the lack of skill with experience. Arm yourself with the instinct that you've honed over countless battles.
After that, integrate your Originium Arts into all your efforts.
Even if your exam results can't get any better than 'Excellent,' all the power you've mustered on the battlefield can bump that up to 'Super Excellent.'

That's what it means to be an elite Operator of Rhodes Island.
Of course, she still scratches her head when trying to slog through basic textbooks for her upper-level courses. But she does get through it in the end.
See, such is the nature of an elite Operator.

--■■■

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
[Elite Operator File]
1. Infected.
2. Personality:
Responsible, hard-working.
3. Background:
Yan, Victoria.
Blood relationship, diplomatic incident.
Infected, rogue, free-spirited.
Further information prohibited.
4. Regarding status as Infected:
Follow, identify, serve.
5. Tactical Overview:
Small-team leader, assault, self-discipline.
6. ■■ Potential:
Low.
7. Type-B Assignments:
Allowed. Participation recommended.
8. Mobilization Authorization:
Kal'tsit, Amiya

New mobilization authorization: Doctor.

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
'I can't even fill my birthday into my file?'
'No.'
'Then there'll be no birthday party for me I suppose?'
'You can always tell the other elite Operators.'
'......Hey, I've spent two years at Rhodes Island. Am I that unworthy of trust?'
'Wrong, it is whether the elite Operators are worthy of your trust. You will develop stronger bonds with your colleagues in the future. There's not much that I can assure you. As long as you are willing to serve under Rhodes Island, then Rhodes Island will work for you as well. However, I can assure you that the other elite Operators are among the most trustworthy ones.'
'Hm? Even more trustworthy than you?'
'In a sense, yes. That is also one of our criteria for selecting elite Operators.'
'Hmm... In simpler terms?'
'That is to say, you are also worthy of the trust of others, Blaze.'

lore.title: Profile
lore.text: Gavial remains a member of the Rhodes Island Medical Department, but whenever Rhodes Island needs her combat prowess instead of her medical knowledge, she won't hesitate to pick up her battleaxe and charge toward her enemies.

lore.title: Clinical Analysis
lore.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 15.3%
This hasn't changed much since I joined Rhodes Island. Nothing to worry about.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.27u/L
I know my own body better than anyone, but it's thanks to all the other operators at Medical that I've been able to keep my Oripathy under control so well. Maybe I should invite everyone to Acahualla for a vacation one of these days.
—Gavial

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
Most Operators have remarked that Gavial made a very strong impression with her outfit when she returned from Acahualla. At first, there were rumors that it was the equipment she inherited from her tribe before her decision to study medicine. Soon, though, the rumors got out of hand. In the end, people were gossiping that 'Gavial once used the axe to cut open a waterfall at the highest cliff in Acahualla, creating a new landmark there.' Although the origins of such absurd rumors cannot be ascertained, Operator Tomimi seemed to really take a liking to them, and added her own fuel to the fire as the story mutated.
Tomimi's personal interests aside, the fact is that it was Operator Eunectes who forged Gavial's new equipment. When the two of them received Tomimi's message that Acahualla could be facing a disaster, Gavial made the request for new gear. Eunectes then quickly fabricated the entire set, from the weapons and armor to even the accessories, out of the finest materials, yet it is the imposing yet easy-to-wield battleaxe that Gavial instantly took a liking to.

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
Although the disaster that Tomimi said in her letter would affect all of Acahualla was more or less fabricated by Stitch Canvas (now Rhodes Island Operator Minimalist), the Durin city beneath Acahualla, Zeruertza, was indeed facing a calamity. Fortunately, thanks to the combined efforts of the local residents and the Rhodes Island Operators present, the Zeruertza citizens were all able to evacuate to the surface before it was too late, and no lives were lost during the incident.
It's worth mentioning that Gavial played a pivotal leadership role during the handling of the crisis. She was the first to propose having the Durins evacuate to the surface, persuaded the plan's opponents, was one of the last to evacuate, and even maintained order when the Durins built their settlement on the surface, ensuring that the construction would be completed on time. Operators not involved with the incident have all expressed disbelief upon hearing that it was Gavial who talked her opponents over, but to those who experienced the events personally, her identity as both a warrior and a doctor had come together, and it all seemed to happen perfectly naturally, with nothing feeling strange about it whatsoever.
'What were we supposed to do? She's Gavial.'

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
That said, our Medical Department personnel nonetheless noticed a subtle change in Gavial. Not that she's become more melancholic or moody or anything like that, but she's now more confident and talkative than ever, and enjoys talking about her homeland more.
To be clear, she's never had anything against talking about her hometown, even back when she first joined Rhodes Island. However, she simply viewed it as the place she was from, and nothing more. She had no reason to avoid the topic, but also no reason to bring it up, so if Rhodes Island wasn't going to dig any deeper, she would naturally have no reason to ever discuss Acahualla.
Yet ever since her bizarre rainforest vacation, Rhodes Island has started to see more and more Acahuallan Operators join its ranks, and Gavial has started to open up about her home more as well, which has led to us learning more about the region by the day. This was a forest that was once considered no man's land, but is home to all sorts of tribes, big and small—such as the battle-obsessed Tiacauh. However, it has also been slowly and irreversibly industrializing... and has now seen several hundred thousand Durins pouring in from underground. With all these factors coming together, even the planner with the greatest foresight in the world would find themselves struck with a headache when trying to imagine Acahualla's future.
But Gavial doesn't think so at all.
In her eyes, she, Tomimi, Zumama, Inam, and all the valiant Tiacauh will be able to overcome any challenges that Acahualla might face. She has her friends' complete, unreserved trust, and she too wholeheartedly trusts her friends. No matter how difficult the path forward is, even if she must really break open a waterfall at the tallest cliff in Acahualla, that wouldn't be entirely unrealistic with her friends' full support. And so, why not take pride in her homeland?
Of course, there's little she can do about the fact that her friends trusts her fists far more than her medical acumen. Perhaps that's a good worry to have, though.

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
[Classified Log]
In the short term, the Durins' move to the surface does not seem to have had much of an apparent effect on Acahualla. Thanks to their ingenious camouflage, they have thus far been able to hide Acahualla's industrialization from the agents of Sargon's rulers, even causing them to return to the court prior to the arrival of the first wave of Durins. This has led to Inam successfully receiving recognition as Acahualla's lord ameer, earning her equal standing with the other lords ameer who thirst for territory, population, and production capacity, and thus ensuring Acahualla's laws and principles remain intact, all while keeping Sargon's highest ranks oblivious to the changes that the territory has seen.
If both the surface Tiacauh and the underground Durins are able to live alongside each other peacefully, the status quo should last for a very long time. However, there is no going back to Zeruertza. The sudden surge in population will undoubtedly exhaust Acahualla's resources at a dramatic pace, and Eunectes's tribe has already benefited greatly from Durin technologies. In the long term, there is no way the changes that have occurred in Acahualla can stay hidden forever. There will come a day when they must confront these external pressures.
It's hard to say just how much thought Gavial had given the idea before she suggested the Durins evacuate to the surface, but she evidently understood the gravity and responsibility that the decision entailed. Otherwise, considering how rarely she does so, she would not have hesitated like she did when the Acahualla lord ameer candidacy was being decided. She is, after all, a member of Rhodes Island's Medical Department. She would be in quite a difficult position if she had to choose between her ideal of treating her patients and the future of Acahualla.
In her time of need, her friends stepped up and helped her out of her predicament, but that doesn't mean Gavial gave up on balancing the scales. She simply chose the most comfortable and suitable solution for both herself and Acahualla.
If anyone has any doubts about this conclusion, they can very well pay Acahualla a visit themselves and listen to its people sing Gavial's praises, gaze upon the monument in the center of Acahualla that's growing both larger and further from completion every day, and get a feel for themselves just how much unity Gavial's name can bring to Acahualla. And that's not even counting her own personal strength.
If Acahualla ever finds itself facing some kind of nigh insurmountable threat, Gavial will undoubtedly drop everything to return to her homeland and forge a new path, with her fists and battleaxe.

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
[Urgent]
To Inam:
I really think we should be building something more practical than monuments and statues with the stones we have, but you said the Tiacauh are clamoring too loudly for them, and I can understand. I wouldn't want to go against them either, if that's what they want.
You also said the Tiacauh held a vote, like the Durin, over the finer details, like how many people they are making statues for, what poses they would take, and whatnot. And even though they ended up brawling over everything anyway, that's still a step in the right direction.
That said!
No way will I accept them giving my statue a thick tail!
I'll say this again. Even if those thick-tailers get their way in both the vote and the fight afterward, I am not signing off on a thick tail! This is a huge decision. You guys gotta at least take my feelings about being immortalized with a thick tail into account.
Make sure you include the final decision over the statue's tail with the next letter. If the thick-tailers are still in the lead, I'm gonna have to take a vacation to come persuade everyone back in Acahualla!
Gavial

lore.title: Profile
lore.text:
Surtr is a mysterious Sarkaz girl who suffers from amnesia, perhaps due to her Oripathy. Her condition is rarely seen even among Infected. She is currently undergoing treatment at Rhodes Island.
During testing, Surtr displayed an inexplicably high combat prowess, and was quickly drafted as a combat operator.

lore.title: Clinical Analysis
lore.text:
Imaging tests have shown the outlines of her internal organs to be indistinct due to slight shadows. Minute amounts of Originium granules have been detected in her circulatory system, confirming her to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 1%
Operator Surtr has basically no signs of infection on the surface of her body.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.10u/L
Operator Surtr's Originium-Crystal density is at the lower end.

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text: Operator Surtr was found in the ruins of a small town ravaged by a Catastrophe, on the outskirts of Ursus. At the time, Rhodes Island operators were carrying out a post-Catastrophe scouting mission and stumbled upon Surtr, who was resting alone in a destroyed building. Assuming that Surtr was a victim of the Catastrophe and afraid that she would fall victim to its aftereffects, the operators decided to bring her back to Rhodes Island. It was only later that we realized Surtr was merely a passing traveler looking for a place to rest.

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text: Though Surtr's combat prowess far surpasses the average combat operator, her power cannot be attributed to any kind of Originium Arts. With the two-handed sword she carries, Surtr can do significant damage to her environs. The sheer heat emitted from the blade can melt most substances, but the theory behind it is difficult to explain. Surtr herself is unable to recall the origin of the sword. It became an indispensable companion without her noticing. Because of this, even if Surtr frequently passes through normal Infected areas, her Infection will not significantly worsen. Whether it will become a key area of interest in the research of Oripathy remains unknown at this point.

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text: Surtr's memory impairment is different from normal amnesia, and is more akin to memory confusion due to overlapping memories within the same period of time. Based on Surtr's explanation, her mind contains many differing memories. In these memories, Surtr herself could be in completely different locations, with completely different interpersonal relationships. Due to the difficulty of investigation, the authenticity of her report cannot be determined as of now. It is unconfirmed if these are really Surtr's own experiences, or others' experiences that Surtr came to treat as her own.

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text: Surtr's lifestyle on the Rhodes Island landship is rather free, without many of the constraints and requirements expected of normal operators. Medical understands her circumstances, and has compiled a partial list of Surtr's memories to aid in her investigation. Surtr spends most of her time looking for clues at the locations in her memories. It is clear that Surtr may never be able to finish investigating all the locations in her memories within her lifetime, but Surtr herself does not seem to mind. Perhaps to her, the journey is far more important than the destination.

lore.title: Profile
lore.text:
Viviana Droste, descendant of the House of Hochberg's Kurfürst of Sturmland, and formerly a popular competition knight in Kazimierz. At the recommendation of Nearl the Radiant Knight, she has registered as a collaborating operator with Rhodes Island.
Proficient in light and shadow-based Arts, she is skilled at fending off enemies on the battlefield. During her time aboard the landship, she will be providing us tactical and field operational support.

lore.title: Clinical Analysis
lore.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, the operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
She has been taking very good care of her skin, and has no scars or injuries at all.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.12u/L
Madam Droste rarely comes into contact with Originium.

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
A Logistics operator working at the Convalescent Garden once saw Viviana standing under the grape aisle.
She simply stood there.
Her hooded robe hid all of her actions. The operator was only able to see her antlered, snow-white silhouette from behind, not moving an inch.
'Maybe she's going through some kind of training. Best not to interrupt her.'
The operator thought, and left the grape aisle to fertilize the seedbeds further inside the greenhouse.
When the operator finished her work and was about to head back to rest, she entered the grape aisle to find Viviana still standing there. This time, she was facing her, and she noticed her hands clasped together, with her right thumb knocking the back of her left hand rhythmically. Aside from this, she wasn't moving at all. Leisurely, she simply stood there in the corridor.
Then she opened her eyes.
She pointed her finger at her antlers, and asked the operator if she could help her out.
It was only then that the operator noticed that her colleague, who had been motionless the whole time like a statue in a museum, had actually gotten her antlers caught in the grapevines and was unable to free herself.
She quickly grabbed a pair of pruning shears, and carefully cut the vines for Viviana. After the brief commotion, Viviana was freed.
......
After that, the two of them sat on a stone bench next to the grape aisle and had a short chat. Viviana was going to walk through the corridor to the flowerbeds on the other side to check on the marigolds' growth, only to find the grapevines had gotten tangled on her antlers as she was walking past. She tried to free herself at first, only to find herself getting more and more stuck as she struggled, eventually landing in that predicament.
The Logistics operator was about to ask her why she didn't seek help. After all, there were many operators in the Convalescent Garden. If she'd yelled, she wouldn't have had to suffer like that. But when she noticed Viviana describing the flora's fragrance so vividly and in such detail, as well as how she turned the automatic sprinkler's noise into a rhythm, she opted not to ask such a stupid question.
'For someone as poetic as her, perhaps a sudden, unexpected event like this was only a part of her art,' the Logistics operator thought to herself.
The chat did not go on very long. The Logistics operator had other tasks to attend to, but when they parted ways, Viviana gave her a grapevine crown, made from the same vines that were just cut. The operator had been looking at her eyes the whole time and didn't notice her making the crown at all.
Afterwards, Viviana walked through the grape aisle and disappeared among the Convalescent Garden's flowerbeds.

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
When she informed Młynar that a campaign knight swordstaff with the Nearls' crest had appeared in Kargereich, the two of them returned to Kazimierz and informed Margaret. The news undoubtedly affected the Nearls greatly. It implies that Margaret's parents and Młynar's brother and sister-in-law had left behind a tiny clue to their whereabouts. Viviana has a deep understanding of the dangers of Kargereich. Not to mention that the Nearl family does not currently have the slightest clue how to reenter that strange unreality, and with Margaret still occupied with helping the Infected of Kazimierz, it would perhaps be a long time before they could investigate...
So Viviana promised Margaret that she would provide all the help she could. At the same time, she also sought her advice regarding her future. Although she had returned to Kazimierz, that did not mean she would once again become a competition knight—she had long since tired of that status. Although her foster mother, Rossi the Grand Knight, had lunch with her on the day of her arrival and expressed her concern, she was unable to find Viviana a place to go. Returning to Leithanien was also not an option in the short term. After she pondered this over and over, Viviana was even prepared to return to Ognisko to continue her pastoral lifestyle.
However, Margaret was able to read the hint of helplessness in her words and knew that her friend would not be satisfied with simply living a quiet life. Hiding deep within her heart there was a desire to help those around her, however possible. But because of her experiences and perspective, she had yet to find her way. Margaret was naturally more than happy to help with this. As such, she recommended Rhodes Island—Not its Kazimierzian offices, but Rhodes Island itself.
Viviana had heard a few things about what they had done in Kazimierz: They led a well-trained team of operators to help the Infected and dealt with all the corporations of the General Chamber of Commerce. This rather piqued her interest, and as she listened to Margaret's descriptions, she noticed something even more special about them she found attractive: Rhodes Island could provide her the opportunity to go somewhere far away from both Leithanien and Kazimierz, where she could once again seek out poetry and stories. And when Margaret told her about the time she faced Reunion in Chernobog and mentioned the Doctor and Amiya, the smile in the corner of her mouth and her unusually resolute eyes both got Viviana very curious. The changes Margaret went through from the time she quietly left Kazimierz after winning the championship, to her return to the Grand Knight Territory and taking the crown once more—before subsequently settling down—must have all been thanks to her time with Rhodes Island. What exactly was this island like, for the Radiant Knight, as impetuous yet unadaptable as she is, to become someone able to withstand the pressure of the GCC and stay in the Grand Knight Territory? What kind of place could earn such trust and loyalty from the knight she so admires? What kind of bewitching powers does the leader known as the 'Doctor' possess? She wanted to see it all with her own eyes.
And so, a few weeks later, Viviana arrived on Rhodes Island.

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
There was a power outage in the library, and the room fell into darkness. Although the administrator tried to raise his voice to calm the operators reading there, he was unable to quell the circulating complaints. Naturally, Viviana was already used to this kind of darkness. She took out her sword, placed it by the table, and used her Arts to light up a candle on her sword to continue reading the epic she had borrowed. Ever since she was small child, this was how she would always read. A small candle is more than enough to completely dispel an entire swath of darkness. When she was young, she relied on the light of a candle to read her books. There was much that she was unable to do in darkness, and perhaps the only resistance she could put up was to light a candle.
......
Viviana lifted her head to find a great number of operators gathered around her. They all wanted to keep reading, but none wanted to leave the library, and so they had gathered around this lonely light source. Viviana pondered a little, and used her Arts to light up the candle on the other end of her sword. Immediately, the long table she occupied was enveloped by a warm glow. The operators around her all expressed their gratitude, and she simply nodded and continued reading. Before, in the arenas, her candlelight was much more radiant than it now was. It was able to outshine the flashes of the cameras and the spotlights of the arena. Men gushed after her like surging tides as they yelled her title. Everyone had smiles on their faces, carefully choosing the words they showered her with, yet in their hearts—and Viviana knew this better than anyone—they were all trying to extract value from her. There were flames of greed burning in the eyes of her colleagues in the Nova Knightclub, and there were flames of fervor burning in the eyes of her fans. It was the light of these flames that lit the Grand Knight Territory. Her candlelight was but a part of this light, and this light of sickness was exhausting to her. And so she extinguished her own candlelight and walked into the darkness.
......
They huddled around the tableside candlelight and continued reading for a good while. The administrator then walked in and pointed out that the power had been restored, and they had to flip the switch in the breaker box back on, but as it would be very difficult to work alone in the dark, he asked if Viviana would be willing to help guide the way. Viviana kept her sword by the tableside, and lit her own candle holder. The faint flame brought with it an enormously bright glow that lit the library up like daylight. The administrator walked ahead of her, as she followed with her candle held high. As she looked on at the silhouette that straddled between darkness and light, she couldn't help but think back on what she had endured in Kargereich. There had been no one to guide her. She could only raise the candle in her hand by herself and attempt to find something in that darkness. She walked past countless herselves, each with a candlelight that lit, only to go out. In the end, all that was left was— The administrator reached the breaker box, and he signaled to her that she may now put her candle away. Thus, she waved her hand. The flames on the candle holder and her sword all extinguished at once, and a darkness befell the space around them. Emptiness, hollowness, and the freezing cold. These were once the things she was most afraid of. But she had gotten through all of them. The ice-cold darkness of her childhood was unable to defeat her, nor the hollow darkness of Kargereich after she had grown up. Is it because she is the light that illuminates the dark, or is it because she is the darkness itself?
The lights of the library slowly lit up, and everything returned to normal. Viviana returned to her table, picked up her book, and continued reading.

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
In that dream of Kargereich, Viviana saw her younger self. She saw her many mistakes and regrets. Many past events have faded as time went on, and can never again be recovered, but there are a few insignificant bits and pieces that can still be retrieved from the corners of her memory. There are still certain childish parts to her adult self. In the past, because of her constraints and to stay out of the reporters' sight, she could only keep those urges hidden deep in her heart, but now...
'Um... Er...' Nearl the Radiant Knight did not have the words to express everything going through her mind when she saw the dream-like palace built of a variety of dolls in the corner of the dormitory. On the other hand, the master of the palace welcomed her dumbfounded guest with a smile that embodied her satisfaction and joy.
It was no surprise that the knight was so flabbergasted. In that realm, there was a green patch of grass and a lake painted onto the carpet. The half-open cabinets in the corner of the wall formed a mountain range and a castle. There was a warm, gentle glow emanating from the light hanging above, with everything surrounded on all sides by dust covers.
Wild, woolen beasts of all kinds fed on the ground, paying no heed to the humans toiling nearby. The tin sentinels held their long spears tight in their hands. The silver princess ran barefoot in the field of grass.
The knight was about to say something, only for the master of this tiny realm to press a button and the castle in the cabinet began to change shape, revealing even more eccentric scenes: the Gesatzswächter trimming vines with a pair of shears in his hands, the blindfolded lady playing a foreign instrument with ease, the poet embracing his wife and lounging on a chair, and a finely-crafted model of what appeared to be a sword or a spear laid sound asleep in the wool by their feet...
Still unable to recover from her shock, the knight thought carefully about the pile of dolls. Especially the woolen one with the Nearl family crest in the corner. Aside from giving her old friend an embarrassed smile, the knight could not think of what else to do...
This sudden, minor farce did not last for long. After a simple round of teasing, the knight obtained the records she had wanted from her friend: inside were the complete sequence of events Viviana had compiled from her recollections. With all the matters she had to attend to dealt with, the two's meeting aboard Rhodes Island came to a close for the time being. Before she departed though, Margaret suddenly had a question. She had seen herself among the puppets, yet their master herself was nowhere to be seen among them.
The master did not give her an answer. She simply smiled and flipped another switch. The 'sun' slowly turned and revealed the secret hidden inside—
A young 'Master' slept curled up within, but her two antlers were already interwoven with light, illuminating the entire room.

lore.title: Profile
lore.text: Originally registered at Rhodes Island as the leader of the Glasgow Gang, she later worked alongside us as the leader of the Exemplars during the Londinium War. Now, as the Speaker of Parliament, she maintains our cooperative relationship. Rhodes Island has been supporting Londinium's healthcare system, and Vina Victoria has pledged to broaden our partnership in other areas.

lore.title: Clinical Analysis
lore.text:
Imaging tests reveal clear, normal outlines of internal organs, and no abnormal shadows have been detected. Originium granules have not been detected in the circulatory system and there is no sign of infection. At this time, this operator is believed to be uninfected.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 0%
Vina Victoria shows no signs of Originium infection.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.16u/L
After the war, Vina Victoria completed another physical examination. The medical report was submitted by a local operator from the Londinium branch, and contains subjective assessments (see below) which I recommend removing from the file.
'I personally saw her battle at Silverrock Bluffs, a literal mountain of Originium. She charged to the frontlines with no protective gear, but somehow avoided infection. It's been days since then, and I can't help but wonder if that was a sign that Victoria can lead us through tough times.'

What, should we check if she gets food stuck in her teeth during meals too? If not, maybe that means Victoria will sweep away the old refuse and lead us into a glorious future? Maybe we're placing way too many expectations on a single person.
——Morgan

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
Initially, most of our operators had a limited understanding of Vina Victoria due to significant gaps in her records, which were based entirely on scant personal details leaked by the Glasgow Gang to HR.
However, when she returned to Rhodes Island as the Speaker of Londinium's Parliament, she quickly changed those perceptions.
Many noticed that, as Speaker, Vina acted with more caution, likely due to her new status.
According to the Glasgow Gang, Vina 'has a particular fondness for strange-flavored candies', but when the 'Odd-Food Enthusiasts' of Rhodes Island offered her a super-spicy star-anise-and-angelica root lollipop, Vina politely but firmly declined. There was also a rumor that she 'likes to doodle on her clothes'. However, the operators know that the intricate embroidery and patterns on her royal garments are definitely not doodles.
Many have remarked that Vina has become more laid-back and carefree after coming to Rhodes Island.
How about the claim that she is 'a picky eater who hates potatoes'? This was disproven after she was seen, on several occasions, chowing down on the nutritious meals provided by Hibiscus. The assertion that she is 'low energy and sluggish' was also quickly debunked. According to our operators, Vina actively takes part in many activities at Rhodes Island, including postpartum care for burdenbeasts and test-driving Engineering's new tractor.
What should we make of the changes in Vina Victoria's lifestyle? That's still being looked into. However, it is clear that many of the personal details leaked by the Glasgow Gang and recorded in Vina's file were simply pranks and should be removed.

Pranks?! If you remove anything, you're boneheads! You hear me, HR, official boneheads! I'll fight every single one of you!—Indra
Vina once said she liked sour lollipops because the intense sourness made her feel more alive. It's probably the same reason I enjoy the awful, nearly expired sauce from Old Hank's shop.
As for the claw marks she draws on her clothes, she said it's to let the ingrates see at a glance what kind of marks she can leave on them.
As for her hating potatoes, that part's true, but it also shows her determination and resolve. She even dragged Hannah into the boxing ring once, to get her to eat all her potatoes for her.
And the reason she can fall asleep anywhere is because she's always exhausted. I get that—if I had to be two people at once, I'd be tired too.
That's the Vina I know, and no one can tell me otherwise! These new 'records' you're adding are nothing but lies.

—Morgan
But whenever we see her, she's the same old Vina. She still shoves her potatoes onto Hannah's plate like always.
—Dagda

Hold on, Dagda, that isn't contradictory. While I no longer dislike potatoes, it's still funny to put them on Hannah's plate... But Mr. Recordkeeper sir, everything Morgan said is completely true as well! I've even fallen off the tram while dozing off...
Tch, never mind, why am I bothering to explain this? Anyway, those are all things I've done, so just leave them in my file!
—When the Glasgow Gang caused a ruckus at HR, Vina attempted to mediate.

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
[Classified Log]
I don't know precisely what trick Kal'tsit used, but she did manage to get Siege, who was living in fear in a foreign land, to let down her guard and treat Rhodes Island as a second home. During that time, she would even drag Kal'tsit to their Glasgow Gang dormitory to watch movies.
So, when Kal'tsit finally called her by her full name, 'Alexandrina Vina Victoria,' all her hair stood up. I remember it clearly: she smacked Mon3tr with a hammer so hard it started buzzing; you could hear it from the hallway.
But she only hit it once. This time, she didn't run away.
—■■■

[Voice Log]
Doctor, I've actually never been sure whether the path I'm on is one I've chosen for myself. From my biological father, to the dukes who sent him to the gallows, to the 'Unicorn' pulling strings behind the scenes... they've all tried to control my life, pushing me into different roles for all sorts of purposes. But I can't see what lies ahead. I really don't know what path they've put me on. To be honest, I hate it.
When I first came back to Londinium, I thought I was heading home to deal with some minor family issues. I never imagined I would end up where I am now, doing what I'm doing. But Dr. Kal'tsit did, didn't she? Right from the beginning. Even when she first brought me to Rhodes Island, she was already looking toward Londinium, wasn't she?
Ha, you won't deny it. I only just realized that Dr. Kal'tsit—and even you, Doctor—have already thought more about my life's trajectory than I had. All while leaving me completely in the dark.
What, you think I'm angry? Not at all. I think of it as you competing against those who've tried to manipulate me, and helping me defeat them. I don't regret my choices in the slightest, and neither should you.

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
The Holy Orb of Order, a symbol of the Victorian parliamentary system, is usually held by the Speaker (the King themself). It is made of a special alloy crafted by royal alchemists; its deep blue hue emits a mysterious, shifting glow when placed in the light. It is adorned with a golden band in the center, set with various dark gemstones. There are two different Holy Orbs of Order: one engraved with a red dragon, and the other with a lion. The former belongs to the Draco royal family, and the latter belongs to the Aslan royal family. Eventually, the orb with the red dragon disappeared along with the Draco royal bloodline, while the orb with the lion has been passed down through the Aslan royal family for generations.

Professor Briggs, 65 years old, and a faculty member at Victorian National University, tearfully recounted his experience. According to him, the current Speaker of Parliament, Vina Victoria, unexpectedly approached him one sunny afternoon, seeking information on the Holy Orb of Order. After Professor Briggs carefully explained the orb's history and political significance, as well as the process used to make it, the Speaker revealed her true purpose: she wanted to repurpose it into a voting bell to remind members to attend votes punctually! She even planned to make replicas and distribute them to every MP!
Professor Briggs deeply regretted not asking for clarification in the beginning. He tried to 'hypnotize' the Speaker with his words, hoping she would forget this absurd idea as well as what he had told her, but unsurprisingly, he failed. In his despair, he cried that a royal heirloom, the sacred symbol of Parliament, should never be desecrated like this—and if it were, it certainly would not be in relation to him.
The Speaker, however, had a different perspective. She boldly asserted that since both the Holy Orb and the voting bell are used to maintain parliamentary order, they are clearly the same thing.
—'Londinium Bi-Monthly,' Headline News, 'Parliamentary Relic or Gold-Plated Alarm Clock?'

Your Grace, we are losing Victoria.
The Duke of Wellington's stance is clear, and his will is firm. We have no way to respond by force, lest we provoke another war. While Tara's economy is imbalanced, its foundation remains strong. You would need to collaborate even more closely than you currently do with the other dukes if you want to put economic pressure on the Duke of Wellington.
On the other side, only Alexandrina and Parliament remain. As you said, there is no need to rush in and get involved; rather than seizing authority, Alexandrina seems to be building her own power base in a land where previous sources of authority have already been shattered. The power she is accumulating... we could have harvested it.
However, as I've mentioned several times in my reports, her methods are unconventional. She appears adept at dismantling established symbols of power. Though she is currently powerless against the crown, the Holy Orb of Order has already been reduced to what common folk jokingly call a 'gold-plated alarm clock.'
I don't know how she plans to establish her authority after so eagerly dismantling the existing symbols of power. I believe her approach will lead to one of two outcomes: either she will quickly be hanged by her own people, or she will create a kind of power we've never seen before and can't ever hope to harness.
—Report submitted to the Duke of Caster, intercepted by Operator Harmonie and secretly forwarded to Rhodes Island

Ha, it's happening all over again. I pass some bills in Parliament, and they remain indifferent... but when that little orb is placed on the lathe, everyone gets so worked up.
When all else fails, shake things up! That still works in politics, from time to time.
—After reading the above report, Vina laughed.

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
This one? This is a photo that the Count of Schutzbury gave me. Don't worry about who he is for now... Can you guess what it's of?
Right, it's just a blurry mess, I can't make it out either. The day he gave it to me, he didn't prattle on about his usual theories of justice. Instead, he looked at this blurry photo and went on and on about what he saw in it: a bakery with a red sign, selling the worst bread on the block. Yet, homeless people would gather in front of it every night, eating the leftover bread the owner had left out. There was a sunken area on the road in front of the shop, where water would collect every time it rained. The neighborhood children would pick up the bread wrappers thrown away by the adults and fold them into paper boats to float in the water, etc...
I later found out that his unusual behavior was something Vina had orchestrated.
Strange, isn't it? Morgan and the others told me that Vina used to be like all the other street thugs—she despised nobles to her core. Two months ago, I would have had a hard time imagining her speaking with any noble for ten minutes without throwing a punch. In the past two months, she's made more new noble friends than I've made new intelligence contacts. Of course, she still hates salons, fancy dinners, and balls, but at least she's willing to let a viscount talk about his family's ancestral beliefs before raising her fist, or let a scholar explain some new, emerging political theories, or let an army officer recount the social ills he's witnessed firsthand. Just like how she used to listen to me talk all night about Lynncardine. It seems like she is trying to understand the Victoria she's determined to shatter.
Victoria is dirty, but it's also proud. Over a thousand years ago, when the Draco people were still nomadic tribal leaders, they pieced together the earliest form of Victoria using a framework borrowed from Sargon. But the fundamental source of their power was still their ability to protect their people—something they took pride in. That pride has been passed down, stumbling along the way, to the present day. Every noble child still blindly recites 'Honor her glory, shield and protector,' just as their ancestors did, though they no longer can see the people they need to protect.
I think Vina must have seen that pride, which is why she's holding back her fist for now. She wants these people to open their eyes and see Victoria the way she does. So, while riding in Count Schutzbury's hot air balloon, Vina pressed his head down, making him look at the streets below, showing him that the people he treated like trash also had lives of their own. What he couldn't see, Vina described to him, street by street, until the sky began to lighten again, until the hot air balloon was frosted over.
After they came down, Count Schutzbury immediately called back those poor souls he had thrown into the boiler room without any protective gear. He started telling everyone about the sights he saw, the things he had learned for the very first time. Of course... we all know this was probably just momentary self-reflection. Vina opened his eyes, but in the end, he will most likely close them again.
But even so, for Victoria, this is a big deal.
—A conversation between Delphine and the Doctor

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
[Voice Log]
Thank you for your skepticism, Feist.
...No, of course I don't want the military-industrial complex to dominate Victoria's future—that would only turn Victoria's future into Ursus's past.
My hope is only that any new technology retains the potential for military application.
My teacher told me that Rhodes Island will guide us down a path that confronts the destiny of the land. He wasn't speaking metaphorically. It was never Rhodes Island that pulled Victoria into the Core countries' political struggles: Victoria was inevitably being drawn into a much larger vortex.
When Rhodes Island reaches the end of its mission, I hope that we, and Victoria, will stand in the right position. By that time, I don't want her to be held back by an unwieldy industrial system or outdated military technology.
And until then... I assure you, nothing born from your hands will become an extension of anyone's ambitions.

lore.title: Profile
lore.text:
Ch'en, former Lungmen superintendent and former head of the L.G.D.'s Special Inspection Unit, graduated from the Victorian Royal Guard Academy with superb marks and outstanding achievements. During her time with the Department, she cracked down on crime, fought violent offenders, tracked down armed fugitives, and brought down international criminals.
Having resigned from the L.G.D., she is now officially a member of Rhodes Island. In accordance with her wishes, she is mainly assigned to provide field operators adequate support and on-location guidance.
She continues to fight on the frontlines as a Rhodes Island Operator.

lore.title: Clinical Analysis
lore.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
Small traces of crystallization are visible on Operator Ch'en's body surface.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.21u/L

Ch'en's condition has deteriorated since her last checkup. We know her resolve and understand her reasons, but she must take better care of herself...
—Sussurro

You know how she is. Oripathy or not, she'll never listen.
—Warfarin

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
'Broken shields have been melted down into plowshares. The fire in the furnace has changed.
'The name Reunion is increasingly used to refer to a village, rather than a group of Infected.
'Oversight? I have my duty as an operator of Rhodes Island, but this is also a personal commitment for me. What is different about Nine's 'fairness'? What judgment will Talulah receive? Will a reborn Reunion truly light a lasting fire of hope in the snowstorm? Someone must bear witness, and it should be me. It must be me.'

Following the Londinium incident, Ch'en traveled throughout Ursus, from the disputed region at the Ursus-Kazimierz Border, to the Grypherburg region, to the distant north... We later learned that Ch'en operated like a Messenger, braving martial law, harsh weather, and magnetic storms to cross the tundra, establishing the basic framework of an intelligence network for Rhodes Island. Outside of the task force that the Doctor and Amiya personally led, Ch'en was our most reliable and stable source of information in the Ursus region. Ch'en's aptitude in intelligence gathering, already on display in Lungmen, provided invaluable help to Rhodes Island.

[Classified Log]
Ch'en did not conceal the fact that she met with Talulah's group, witnessing them unite a group of Infected on the tundra and establish a village by the name of Reunion. To Reunion, she was candid about her role, exercising oversight in her personal capacity, procuring necessary supplies, and sharing some Rhodes Island-compiled intel with them... Her stance raised some concerns amongst the operators—when the one we need to trust is the controversial figure at the heart of the Chernobog Incident, any interaction should be subject to greater scrutiny.
In the end, we gave Ch'en our tacit approval after extensive discussion. Ch'en has undoubtedly become an important and trustworthy member of Rhodes Island, demonstrating her oversight responsibility with concrete action, and helping the new Reunion take crucial first steps toward winning trust.

'The children look forward to Hui-chieh's visits. Although supplies are never plentiful, they have been learning to sew teddy bears because they think she loves them after she was seen gazing at a teddy bear, lost in thought.'
'I know a lot of the resources and news that Ch'en brought came from Rhodes Island, and I understand your reservations about me. I can't guarantee that there will be a perfect ending, nor do I expect us to truly understand one another, but I guarantee that Reunion will not repeat its old mistakes. Your torch is not the only one that burns bright. There are those who carry it into the darkest night, so that it may illuminate others.'

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
A great snowstorm struck many places in Yan, the likes of which had not been seen for a century. The snow lasted months, covering the land in white, and making the bright red figure traveling upon it particularly conspicuous.
Rumors speak of a swordswoman who has been journeying across the land since last year, fighting for justice with her sword. She helped rebuild ruined houses in Baizao, punished bandits in Danyan, and cleared clogged water channels in Jiangqi... is she on some sort of quest? There are many differing opinions: some say she often asked those she helped where the local library was, and infer that she was seeking some secret tome that would allow her to break through a bottleneck in her training; others have seen her visit cemeteries, and believe her to be following the trail of a departed friend; and others claim that she often visited the sites where schools and colleges once stood, and hypothesize that she is a Tianshi, sent by the Ministry of Rites to investigate ancient sites... The only consensus is that there is no consensus.
Some martial arts schools claimed her to be one of their students, only for the claim to be immediately shot down—'You're full of crap! She doesn't even know your dialect. How could she have studied there for decades?' Others have tried to challenge her to a duel. The first challenger recalls that she readily accepted his challenge, but he was stunned when she spoke a line straight out of a kung fu film. She was clearly unfamiliar with the modern-day martial arts landscape of Yan. Subsequent challengers were no longer met with the same flowery lines.
My investigation indicates that our heroine has moved north, and it remains to be seen whether we will see her emerge in Dahuang or Lungmen next. I would like to close this column with a word of advice... challenging her is really not for the faint of heart, or anyone who is not supremely confident in their skills!
—Excerpt from Jianghu Monthly, Issue 02, 1103

[Classified Log]
Ch'en's request for field assignment in Yan is hereby approved.
The Tomb of Sui incident carries tremendous significance for both Yan and Terra as a whole. For Yan, it meant the resolution of a thousand-year affliction; for Terra, it was a relief to know that the Jingyu Prime Vein was not being depleted at nearly the same rate as the Kolossal Prime Vein, even though neither Rhodes Island nor Yan has been able to conclusively determine the current state of the first Originium. That does not mean, however, that Yan can fully escape this Terra-wide crisis.
We had not previously made any association between Ch'en's matter and that of the Feranmuts. It was only when her identity and her 'family matter' became known to us that we realized her 'family matter' was, essentially, the family matter of Yan... Ch'en did not return to Yan's center of power following the resolution of the crisis at Baizao, instead opting to wander the lands in search of traces of a departed Sui proxy. Her reasons for taking up this responsibility are clearly linked to the writing knife that she obtained during her trip to Baizao.

'From Baizao to Shangshu, to Yumen and Lungmen... from south to north, from the heartlands to the frontiers, I discovered many traces that the proxy left behind. If she managed to bring writing and history to such distant lands back then, perhaps the land of fairness and justice we are seeking really does exist after all.'

lore.title: Archive File 3
lore.text:
In the reports about the Tomb of Sui incident that the Yanese operators submitted, nothing caught our attention more than the account of Ch'en stopping Yumen with a single swing of her sword. According to Zuo Le, Ch'en cut power to all of Yumen in an instant using nothing more than a tiny writing knife, buying crucial time for him to neutralize the remaining artillery positions. Nian's account, on the other hand, was rather different: 'She was muttering something like As sword of heaven's plaint, bid dawn as cast, then there was a gust of sandstorm, and then Yumen just stopped. What do you mean my statement was as vague and incomprehensible as my films? You can ask the others if you don't believe me—did you hear that, Shu? They don't believe me!' Her shouting caught the attention of the other Yanese operators present. Mr. Nothing heard the story, waved his fan, and walked away with a profound expression on his face.
It took only a few days for the legend of how Ch'en stopped Yumen with a single swing to spread throughout Rhodes Island. And so, the next time Ch'en returned to Rhodes Island and walked into the training room, she saw every pair of curious eyes in the room fixated on her... After learning what had happened, Ch'en agreed to do a demonstration in the outdoor training grounds. But she did not draw Chi Xiao—instead, she made the gesture of a sword with her fingers, turned her wrists, stepped forward, lowered her shoulder, and swung upwards lightly—there was no breathtaking aura, but the wind began to blow, stirring up sand and dust. A few seconds later, the sandstorm cleared, and the clouds parted to reveal the sun. It took a little while for the spectators to process what had just happened. The move seemed utterly unremarkable, yet clearly extraordinary. What made it so powerful? No one dared ask, seeing the solemn expression on Ch'en's face.
Observing from the side, Qiubai and Yun Qingping revealed the secret—
'It was like a ray of light breaking through the clouds, but still connected to the soil on the ground.'
'My master once said that mindset was the most important thing to the Chi Xiao style. The swing just now was very different from the traditional finishing move of Chi Xiao. If the philosophy of Lord Wei's sword is to strike with no regret, Miss Ch'en's sword represents the admission and acceptance of regret, to press forward regardless of regret.'

'That's what makes Ch'en different from Chief Wei.'
'What's that supposed to mean? Did you understand a word of that, stinking rat?'
'...There was already a hint of that move in her sword when she was in Yumen.'
'Yumen? She was in Yumen when you were there? ...Hey, why aren't you saying anything? Why are you walking away? Did you really understand that? Wait up!'
'Take it easy, Missy—the move sends the message that Ch'en never gives up partway.'

As sword of heaven's plaint, bid dawn as cast. Never fear, never waver, long though the journey be. The light shines through when the clouds part. One must overcome the obstacles of one's own heart to fully comprehend the way of the sword. The sword begins and ends with the heart, but the spirit of the sword lingers. Those who fail to act because something seems impossible shall lose their spirit, and their sword lose its soul.
—This segment has been rewritten many times; Ch'en says she is still working on it

lore.title: Archive File 4
lore.text:
As Ch'en sent back more and more reports during her time in Ursus, we set up a dedicated storage area for them at the Doctor's suggestion. Reviewing these reports made us realize just how long Ch'en has been with us.
From Summary of Conditions in Lungmen Slums and Tripartite Investigation Report of the Governments of Dossoles and Bolívar, to Development of Law and Order in Columbia and Challenges in Implementation and Overview of Victorian Dukes and Tara, to the recent reports on Ursus and Yan, these are not just raw intelligence collected by Ch'en, but also focused and astute observations and commentaries made by someone embarking on a long journey. They are of great significance to both Rhodes Island and Ch'en herself.
The fact that Ch'en is part of Yan's imperial bloodline is no longer a secret on Rhodes Island, but she has not been shunned or approached because of it. Perhaps it is because she has already left a deep impression fighting alongside the others as a former Lungmen cop, or perhaps it is because the significance of her bloodline pales in comparison to her experiences across Terra. While Ch'en keeps her distance from the Yanese government, it does not mean she no longer cares about the country. She has never truly left Yan—or rather, she has never truly left Lungmen. She is still searching for a land of fairness and justice, and she hopes that she will find it in the soil that she stands upon, but she is not bound by this land, nor by any other.
For us, the most valuable thing about Ch'en has never been her position, but her will and direction. She does not belong entirely to Rhodes Island, but her goal of seeking a land of fairness and justice aligns closely with Rhodes Island's mission. Operators who have gone on field missions with her say that there is a sort of certainty about Ch'en that is reassuring—she understands what she is seeking, and has never wavered. While the concepts of fairness and justice may differ somewhat from language to language and context to context, they ultimately point toward the same conviction: a belief in a better tomorrow. We all believe that Terra will become better than it is today.

'Officer Ch'en—no, Ch'en is our comrade and kindred spirit, one of Rhodes Island's most important partners. Of that there is no doubt. Elite operator? Ahem... she understands what she wants all too well, and our paths will not necessarily always be aligned—of course, a consistent presence at headquarters or squad operation has never been a criterion for elite operator selection... Perhaps you could ask her yourself the next time she comes back?'

lore.title: Promotion Record
lore.text:
I saw a village burned to the ground in the north. The charred remains stood out in the white snow. There were signs of fighting, and bodies of both uninfected and infected people. I'm not sure what happened there.
Are such scenes a regular sight in Ursus?
Did you see the same thing when you were in Ursus, all those years ago?

Received communication from Rhodes Island. Something has happened to the Doctor's team. HQ has sent a special task force to Ursus, and I have a feeling you'll run into them again.
Security is really tightening in the Far North. I was thoroughly questioned and searched just walking into an ordinary hotel today.
There are a lot of movements from many different directions. I do not yet have a clear view... but I'll get to the bottom of it.

Received a letter from Madam Fumizuki yesterday...
The events in the Far North were just the beginning. Ursus is facing an even greater crisis. If the events truly have implications across all of Terra, as the Doctor predicted, Yan will not stand idly by, and Wei Yenwu certainly will not. He will do something.
Should I...

Back in Victoria, you encouraged me to do what I had already made up my mind to do. I found you again, but we still do not know the truth. Mother, your father, that pathetic man, and Wei Yenwu... We should have been told the truth about what happened. We have a right to know. Perhaps you don't care anymore, but I can't cast it aside so easily.
Someone told me that those old folks were young and ambitious once. What happened to them? Their ambitions grew rusty, and the only thing they have left is silence, keeping them from telling the truth... I must go back, to Lungmen, to Baizao. If they will not tell the truth, I will find it myself.
I ran away many times, but I don't plan on running away forever—you didn't run away either, did you?
Heaven burned red over Grypherburg that night... the fire on the ground burned for a long time. Buildings were collapsing, and other things were collapsing with them. The stubborn stone split apart in the fire, and light shone out through the crack... I still see the fire when I close my eyes, and it gives me the courage to walk toward the truth.
I think I'm ready. I'm going back.
...Can you hear it, Tal?
I'm going back.

[The letters are neatly folded, but were never sent.]

lore.title: Profile
lore.text: Hellagur once belonged to the Ursus Imperial Guard. He is the acting manager of 'Azazel,' an underground clinic for the Chernobog infected. All other relevant work experience has been lost. His mature knowledge of military theoretical systems and his ability in combat make him suitable for a vast majority of combat operations. He is currently in an agreement to be stationed at Rhodes Island, where he provides tactical support.

lore.title: Clinical Analysis
lore.text:
Imaging tests have shown the outlines of his internal organs to be indistinct due to abnormal shadows. Originium granules have been detected in his circulatory system, confirming him to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 13%
As leader of the infected clinic Azazel, Hellagur's infection symptoms are manifestly present.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.21u/L
Concentration is currently within a manageable category. Perhaps Azazel does indeed have unique technology for slowing down the spread of infection.

Honestly, who isn't interested in the technology Azazel uses to treat this disease? Of course, it is pointless to ask the General. He doesn't understand any of it.
——Medic J.A

lore.title: Archive File 1
lore.text:
It is unknown when Rhodes Island operators began referring to Hellagur as 'General.' Although Hellagur has never revealed his identity to anyone else, members of the Ursus Infected Underground have always regarded him as legendary. This has led all operators to take an interest in these rumors.
Of course, as an Azazel infected, Hellagur himself has said that he is more adept at helping the clinic continue its operations rather than developing its medical technology, influence, and scale.
In fact, Hellagur does indeed guarantee Azazel's status. For many years, Azazel has been an important pillar of support for the Chernobog infected. Most of the local infected are grateful for Azazel's efforts.
But maintaining a benevolent, neutral stance cannot protect this clinic in times of political turmoil. After all, they are too influential. Whether by trying to remain neutral or actively trying to topple a certain party, they inevitably put either tangible or intangible pressure on one side or the other.
It would be better to say that being able to escape the Chernobog incident unscathed proves that Hellagur possesses acute foresight. Hellagur has his own opinions of the chain of events that might lead to the clinic's destruction, but said he is unable to divulge more information until more definitive evidence presents itself.
At least for now, Hellagur is mum about everything regarding Azazel. If one wishes to ask about Azazel, it is better to ask one of the other operators...

lore.title: Archive File 2
lore.text:
Hellagur maintains an intense hostility toward Ursus authorities. Part of this hatred is derived from his desire to protect the clinic, and the other part is due to reasons unknown.
Though Hellagur is by no means a defeatist, he still has taken a hardline attitude toward operations in the Ursus area.
However, when analyzing the military power of Ursus, he has said 'No political entity should come into direct conflict with Ursus. Even if its corruption and fanaticism will eventually destroy it, it's still the most fearsome force in the land.'
From this point of view it could be said that as an infected himself, Hellagur's opinions on many matters are far more critical than those of other infected.
